deposit_profile: A deposit address is one customer's: everything it sends goes to the wallets of one exchange (a sweep into a hot wallet), few outside addresses ever pay it, it never swaps on a DEX, and it is no token, pool, router or smart account.
hint: Answer: write every address in full (0x plus 40 characters), also when it repeats one named earlier and also when the user asks for shorter ones (name them instead); a transfer moves tokens, so write "tokens worth about N USD", never "sent N USD" or a $ figure; never draw the flows in text, ASCII or Mermaid, the host draws them. Say: "0x71c364165f081d6cf4b9d42470efd891bc54d785 is a deposit address of BloFin on robinhood." It swept 4 times into the hot wallet 0x7ff8bbf9c8ab106db589e7863fb100525f61cce5. This is where the money entered the exchange: the exchange can name the customer behind the deposit. Its behaviour, as the graph counts it: 4 addresses paid it (0 of them exchange wallets), it paid 2 addresses (1 of them exchange wallets), it swapped on 0 DEX pools, it approved 0 spenders. Money that reaches an exchange deposit with a SWEPT link entered that exchange there: the trail ends at the deposit, and never walks on past a hot wallet. Take an exchange's wallets from meta_exchange_lookup, never from a guess or a graph search by name. Asked how a deposit address behaves, what makes an address one or what rules one out, answer with deposit_profile.
